title: Cohort-based embedding & rerank sentinel triggered by config/model changes
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Add a lightweight, cohort-oriented sentinel system that runs offline recall/precision and distributional drift checks whenever embedding model versions or reranker configuration flags change. The sentinel is intended to catch regressions from config flips (quantization profile, knn index params, reranker temperature/alpha) before rollout to Dedicated or Private customers. This ticket covers data selection (anchor cohorts), evaluation harness integration, telemetry hooks, and policy wiring to mark config changes as safe/blocked.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Config-driven events trigger a discrete evaluation job against the anchor cohorts within 10 minutes of change. 2) Evaluation computes per-cohort recall@k, mean reciprocal rank (MRR), and embedding cosine shift metrics and emits them to the quality dashboard. 3) Threshold rules (per-cohort and global) are configurable via the model-quality-sentinel project and default to conservative values. 4) If a threshold is breached, the change is tagged as BLOCKED and an automated Slack alert + rollback PR template is created. 5) Runbook created with steps to triage false positives and add new cohorts.
implementation_notes:
- Use existing eval harness from model-quality-sentinel repo; add a lightweight runner that accepts a config-change webhook.
- Anchor cohorts: sample stratified subsets by customer segment, query intent bucket, and input length. Persist cohort ids for reproducibility.
- Metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, normalized cosine drift, and response distribution KL for reranker scores.
- Storage: results stored in BigQuery table `redwood_quality.sentinels` and linked to dashboards.
- Access control: runner runs in the control plane; ensure secrets access follows least privilege for private deployments.
- Performance: evaluation should be limited to 5k examples per cohort initially to bound cost; allow opt-in expansion for enterprise customers.
- Add feature flag to gate automatic blocking behavior during initial ramp.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for runner and metric computations.
- Integration test: simulate config change webhook and assert evaluation kicks off and writes expected rows to BigQuery.
- Shadow run: run sentinel in shadow mode for one week against live config changes before enabling blocking policy.
- Create synthetic regression PRs to verify blocking and alerting behavior.
- Load test: ensure a burst of config changes (100 in 1 hour) queues evaluation jobs without exceeding quota and respects rate limits.
monitoring_plan:
- Dashboards: per-cohort time series for recall@k and cosine drift; heatmap for cohorts vs models.
- Alerts: severity-3 PagerDuty for automated blocking events affecting production customers; Slack channel for ops and PMs for all sentinel alerts.
- Telemetry: tag evaluation runs with change metadata (who, which flag/model, commit) and link to GitHub PR/Change ID.
- Long-term: track false positive rate and adjust thresholds after two weeks of shadow data.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement eval runner and basic cohorts, run locally and in CI. 2) Deploy shadow mode to control plane (no blocking) for 2 weeks; surface results to product and infra. 3) Gradual enable of automated blocking for non-critical flags for internal customers only. 4) After 4 weeks and verified stability, open blocking to all self-serve hosted changes and add opt-in for Dedicated/Private auto-blocking. 5) Formal post-mortem after first real blocked change and iterate on thresholds and cohort composition.
